residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff must be a resident of South Dakota at the time of filing. There is no minimum duration of residency if the cause of action arose in South Dakota.

waitingPeriod.description: South Dakota has no mandatory waiting period, unless the court orders conciliation.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Willful Neglect
fault.description: Willful neglect to provide the common necessities of life

groundsForDissolution.notes: South Dakota allows both fault and no-fault grounds. Irreconcilable differences is the most common ground.

propertyDivision.description: South Dakota follows equitable distribution. The court divides all property of the parties in an equitable manner. The court considers the duration of the marriage, the value of property, the ages of the parties, health, competency to earn a living, and the contribution of each party to the accumulation of property.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: All property is subject to distribution, though the court considers the origin and source of property in determining equitable division.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirements — resident at time of filing
Joint custody; legal and physical custody

filingFees.notes: South Dakota filing fees are approximately $95 for a divorce complaint but may vary by county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Affidavit
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant via sheriff or process server

service.name: Voluntary Appearance and Waiver
service.description: Defendant voluntarily appears and waives formal service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Court order establishing custody and visitation

withChildren.name: Child Support Obligation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per South Dakota Child Support Guidelines (SDCL §25-7-6.2)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per South Dakota Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside South Dakota must file an answer within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: South Dakota uses an income shares model. Both parents' net incomes are combined and child support is determined from the South Dakota Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined net income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: South Dakota courts may award alimony considering factors including the length of the marriage, the earning capacity of each party, the financial condition and needs of each party, the fault of the parties, and any other relevant factors.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request alimony. The court has broad discretion to determine the amount and duration.

court.name: Circuit Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the Circuit Court in the county where either party resides.
